s1.title: Get the proof
s1.lead: This is a report for one spot, measured from orbit. Save it, print it or send the link. A worry is easy to wave away. A dated measurement is not.

read.title: How to read this
read.1: This is a screening estimate, not an inspection. One radar pixel is 80 m wide: it describes the ground under a block, not one building's foundations.
read.2: Buildings are damaged by uneven sinking. The limits 1/500, 1/300 and 1/150 are standard engineering thresholds for the tilt between neighbouring ground. They are counted from the first radar pass, so strain from earlier years is not included.
read.3: Everything after the latest radar pass is a projection that assumes the measured rate continues. Rates change when pumping or rainfall change.
read.4: Only a qualified engineer on site can say whether a building is safe.

s2.title: Send it to someone who must answer
s2.lead: A letter with a measurement attached is treated differently from a complaint. Pick what to ask for, check the text, and send it under your own name.
s2.ask: What do you want to ask for?
s2.ask.inspection.sub: Someone qualified comes to look at the buildings and the ground.
s2.ask.groundwater.sub: How much groundwater is pumped here, what is measured, and what is planned.
s2.to.checked: Contacts gathered from official sources on {date}, without a visit or a phone call. Offices move and numbers change: check before you send.
s2.to.pick: Address the letter to this office
s2.generic.title: We have not looked up the offices for {place} yet. These are usually the ones responsible:
s2.generic.1: The building or public works department of your municipality, or civil protection. They inspect buildings and ground.
s2.generic.2: The water utility or the groundwater regulator. They know how much is pumped and they set the limits.
s2.generic.3: The national or regional geological survey. They monitor the ground.
s2.generic.4: Many countries have a right to information law that obliges public bodies to answer a written request within a set number of days. Search for it with the name of your country.
s2.you.note: What you type here stays on this device. It is only used to fill in the letter.
s2.you.name: Your name
s2.seen.tilt: A building or wall that leans
s2.seen.ground: Cracks or holes in the ground or street
s2.letter.note: You can edit the text before you send it.
s2.right.title: Why they have to answer
s2.urgent.title: If a building looks about to fail
s2.urgent.generic: Do not wait for a letter. Leave the building and call the emergency number.
s2.context.title: What is already known here
s2.tip.title: Make it count
s2.tip.1: Attach the printed report from step 1.
s2.tip.2: Add dated photos of any damage, with a ruler or a coin in the picture for scale.
s2.tip.3: Keep a copy and write down the day you sent it. If nobody replies by the deadline, send it again and say so.
letter.subject.inspection: Request for an inspection: ground sinking measured at {where}
letter.subject.groundwater: Request for information: ground sinking and groundwater pumping at {where}
letter.subject.label: Subject:
letter.intro.noaddress: I live in the neighbourhood described below.
letter.why.inspection: I am writing to ask for an inspection, because satellite measurements show that the ground here is sinking.
letter.why.groundwater: I am writing to ask for information, because satellite measurements show that the ground here is sinking.
letter.ev.spot: Radar measurements by the NISAR satellite of NASA and ISRO show that the ground at {where} sank {sunk} between {from} and {to}. That is a rate of about {rate}.
letter.ev.spot.none: Radar measurements by the NISAR satellite of NASA and ISRO show sinking ground close to {where}.
letter.ev.spot.edge: Radar measurements by the NISAR satellite of NASA and ISRO show that {where} sits on the edge of sinking ground, where neighbouring ground sinks at different rates.
letter.ev.hood: Within {radius} of this point, {sinking} of built up land stands on ground that is sinking or tilting.
letter.ev.hood.fastest: The fastest sinking there is about {fastest}.
letter.ev.hood.buildings: About {buildings} buildings stand on that ground.
letter.ev.limit: If this rate continues, the uneven sinking at this point passes the level at which buildings can start to crack (an angular distortion of 1/500) around {date}.
letter.ev.limit.hood: If this rate continues, about {n} buildings within {radius} will stand on ground that has passed the level at which buildings can start to crack (an angular distortion of 1/500) by {year}.
letter.ev.caveat: These figures are a screening estimate from satellite radar with pixels 80 m wide. They do not replace an inspection on site.
letter.ev.link: The full report, with the map, the method and the data sources, is here: {url}
letter.seen.intro: I have also seen the following myself:
letter.seen.doors: doors or windows that jam or no longer close
letter.seen.tilt: a building or wall that leans
letter.seen.ground: cracks or holes in the ground or the street
letter.ask.intro: I therefore ask you for the following:
letter.ask.inspection.1: An inspection of the buildings and the ground in this area by a qualified engineer.
letter.ask.inspection.2: A written reply with the findings and the measures you plan to take.
letter.ask.inspection.3: Confirmation of whether this area is included in the official risk map and in any monitoring of ground sinking.
letter.ask.groundwater.1: The figures for how much groundwater is extracted in this area and by whom, and how that has changed over the last ten years.
letter.ask.groundwater.2: The official measurements of ground sinking and of groundwater levels for this area.
letter.ask.groundwater.3: The measures planned to reduce the sinking, such as limits on extraction, other sources of water or recharge of the aquifer, and their timetable.
letter.right: I make this request on the basis of: {law}. I ask for a written reply within {deadline}.
letter.right.nodays: I make this request on the basis of: {law}. I ask for a written reply.
letter.noright: I ask for a written reply.
s3.title: Find the others
s3.lead.buildings: About {n} buildings within {radius} of this spot stand on the same moving ground. Most of the people in them have never seen these measurements.
s3.lead.none: Sinking ground is never one household's problem. The cause is shared and so is the fix.
s3.group.title: Join your neighbours
s3.group.none: There is no group for {place} yet. Someone has to start one. It could be you.
s3.group.careful: Do not post your full address or anyone else's in a public group.
s3.kit.title: How a few neighbours become a group
s3.kit.lead: You need three people, not three hundred.
s3.kit.1: Send this report to the neighbours you know. Print it and pin it up in the stairwell or the corner shop.
s3.kit.2: Keep one shared list: address, what is cracked, since when, a dated photo. Ten entries are evidence. One is an anecdote.
s3.kit.3.t: Send one letter with many names.
s3.kit.3: Use the letter from step 2, signed by everyone. One letter with thirty signatures weighs more than thirty letters.
s3.kit.4.t: Bring in people who can amplify it.
s3.kit.4: A local journalist, the engineering or geology department of a nearby university, a residents' association, your councillor. Give them the report: it is checkable.
s3.kit.5: Other cities have stopped their sinking. Ask for the same things, listed below.
